entities.summary: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. The noun "commonwealth", meaning "public welfare, general good or advantage", dates from the 15th century. Originally a phrase, it comes from the old meaning of "wealth", which is "well-being", and was deemed analogous to the Latin res publica. The term literally meant "common well-being". In the 17th century, the definition of "commonwealth" expanded from its original sense of "public welfare" or "commonweal" to mean "a state in which the supreme power is vested in the people; a republic or democratic state".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The concept of a commonwealth has influenced modern democracy and republicanism, shaping the idea of popular sovereignty and citizen participation in governance. Its evolution from a phrase to a distinct political entity reflects the changing understanding of collective well-being and the role of citizens in shaping their own destiny.
